item: Row J R170: the first install reads the seeded rows back once, after the commit that created them
refs: R170; branch claude/v0-5-plan-j8zvre (PR number at push)
summary: A commit expires every row the session holds and each was re-read with its own SELECT: 13,759 of them, 5-6 s, on a first install of the shipped catalogue. seed_sources now reads the table once with populate_existing() right after a commit that created rows, and only then, so a steady boot never runs it and nothing pending can be overwritten. Measured on the real catalogues: first install 10.5 s to 5.6 s plaintext and 10.9 s to 6.2 s encrypted, steady boot unchanged, SQL statements 27,240 to 14,010, row digest identical. tests/test_seed_first_install_refresh.py is red without it.
